21648-westminster.title: Westminster
21648-westminster.creator: Sir Walter Besant
21648-westminster.description: A book by Sir Walter Besant. n the history of London as a whole. These he finished up to the end of the eighteenth century, and they form a record of the great city practically unique, and exceptionally interesting, compiled by one who had the qualities both of novelist and historian, and who knew how to make the dry bones live. The volume on the eighteenth century, which Sir Walter called a "very big chapter indeed, and particularly interesting," will shortly be issued by Messrs.

58201-the-westminster-alice.title: Westminster Alice
58201-the-westminster-alice.creator: Hector H. Munro (“Saki”)
58201-the-westminster-alice.description: A book by Hector H. Munro (“Saki”). “Of course it doesn’t,” the Cat went on cheerfully, “because the unravelling got so tangled that no one could follow it. Its theory is,” he continued, seeing that Alice was waiting for more, “that you mustn’t interfere with the Inevitable. Slide and let slide, you know.”

arxiv-2206-07392.title: Volume Conductor: Interactive Visibility Management for Crowded Volumes Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2206-07392.creator: Žiga Lesar 1, Ruwayda Alharbi 2, Ciril Bohak 1,2, Ondřej Strnad 2, Christoph Heinzl 3, Matija Marolt 1, Ivan Viola 2
arxiv-2206-07392.description: Abstract We present a novel smart visibility system for visualizing crowded volumetric data containing many object instances. The presented approach allows users to form groups of objects through membership predicates and to individually control the visibility of the instances in each group.

arxiv-2206-10248.title: Local structure of convex surfaces near regular and conical points
arxiv-2206-10248.creator: Alexander Plakhov
arxiv-2206-10248.description: Abstract Consider a point on a convex surface in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} , d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 and a plane of support Π \Pi to the surface at this point. Draw a plane parallel to Π \Pi cutting a part of the surface.

arxiv-2311-01346.title: On the Proportion of Coprime Fractions in Number Fields
arxiv-2311-01346.creator: Walter Bridges, Johann Franke, and Johann Stumpenhusen
arxiv-2311-01346.description: Abstract . We determine the asymptotic density of coprime fractions in those of the reduced fractions of number fields. When ordered by norms of denominators, we count a fraction as soon as it “appears” for the first time and no later.

arxiv-2412-14919.title: Computational Aspects of Lifted Cover Inequalities for Knapsacks with Few Different Weights
arxiv-2412-14919.creator: Christopher Hojny, Cédric Roy
arxiv-2412-14919.description: Abstract Cutting planes are frequently used for solving integer programs. A common strategy is to derive cutting planes from building blocks or a substructure of the integer program. In this paper, we focus on knapsack constraints that arise from single row relaxations. Among the most popular classes derived from knapsack constraints are lifted minimal cover inequalities.

arxiv-2508-01368.title: Relation-Aware LNN–Transformer for Intersection-Centric Next-Step Prediction
arxiv-2508-01368.creator: Zhehong Ren, Tianluo Zhang, Yiheng Lu, Yushen Liang, Promethee Spathis
arxiv-2508-01368.description: Abstract Next-step location prediction plays a pivotal role in modeling human mobility, underpinning applications from personalized navigation to strategic urban planning. However, approaches that assume a closed world—restricting choices to a predefined set of points of interest (POIs)—often fail to capture exploratory or target-agnostic behavior and the topological constraints of urban road networks.

arxiv-2508-15862.title: Parameter Estimation of Magnetised Kerr Black Holes Using Their Shadows
arxiv-2508-15862.creator: Heena Ali, Sushant G. Ghosh
arxiv-2508-15862.description: Abstract We investigate the shadow features of magnetized Kerr black holes (MKBHs) using a deviation parameter B B that captures the effect of an external magnetic field on spacetime geometry. These spacetimes, of Petrov type D D and are asymptotically non-flat.

arxiv-2511-20491.title: Семейство римановых задач на группе Гейзенберга
arxiv-2511-20491.creator: Ю.Л. Сачков
arxiv-2511-20491.description: Abstract Аннотация Рассматривается однопараметрическое семейство римановых задач на группе Гейзенберга, сходящееся к субримановой задаче на этой группе при стремлении параметра к предельному значению. Для семейства построен оптимальный синтез, описаны сферы, множество разреза и первая каустика. При стремлении параметра к предельному значению показано, как экспоненциальное отображение, первая каустика, множество разреза и сферы стремятся к соответствующим объектам для субримановой задачи.

arxiv-2602-14796.title: Strongly correlated Josephson junction: proximity effect in the single-layer Hubbard model
arxiv-2602-14796.creator: Don Rolih, Rok Žitko
arxiv-2602-14796.description: Abstract We study the proximity effect in the Hubbard model coupled to BCS superconductors describing a single-layer strongly correlated electron system in a phase-biased Josephson junction. We find two distinct gapped solutions, one Mott-like insulating (M-phase) and one proximitized superconducting phase (S-phase), separated by first-order transition with hysteresis.

pmc-10533873.title: The influence mechanism of industrial policies on Chinese companies' cross-border M&A decision-making
pmc-10533873.creator: Yalan Shen, Mengqi Yang, Hongyu An, Kailun Li
pmc-10533873.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). This study explored the potential links between Chinese industrial policy and cross-border mergers and acquisitions by Chinese firms from 2009 to 2019. Based on describing China's industrial strategy and evaluating the then-current situation of Chinese enterprises' cross-border mergers and acquisitions, this empirical study constructed a two-way fixed-effect panel model and an intermediate effect model to assess the mechanism of industrial policy's influence on Chinese enterprises' cross-border mergers and acquisitions decisions.

pmc-10736511.title: SOCIAL WORKERS AS INFORMAL LEGAL INTERMEDIARIES: RESOLVING CONFLICTING RIGHTS IN NURSING HOMES
pmc-10736511.creator: Angela Perone
pmc-10736511.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Conflicting rights arise often in nursing homes among residents, staff, and family. Nursing home social workers sit at a unique nexus of these rights, given their macro, mezzo, and micro-level training. This study employs a multi-method qualitative design with semi-structured staff interviews (n=90) (direct care, mid-level professional, top management), content analysis of long-term care facility policies (n=376), and ethnographic observation of two facilities (n=8 months) for a multi-layered cross-comparative in-depth case study.

pmc-11441005.title: An automated phenotyping method for Chinese Cymbidium seedlings based on 3D point cloud
pmc-11441005.creator: Yang Zhou, Honghao Zhou, Yue Chen
pmc-11441005.description: Aiming at the problems of low efficiency and high cost in determining the phenotypic parameters of Cymbidium seedlings by artificial approaches, this study proposed a fully automated measurement scheme for some phenotypic parameters based on point cloud. The key point or difficulty is to design a segmentation method for individual tillers according to the morphology-specific structure.

pmc-11647548.title: Balancing CIK Cell Cancer Immunotherapy and PPAR Ligands: One Potential Therapeutic Application for CNS Malignancies
pmc-11647548.creator: Kira Vordermark, JingJing Pu, Amit Sharma, Jarek Maciacyzk, Ingo G H Schmidt‐Wolf
pmc-11647548.description: BackgroundCytokine‐induced killer (CIK) cell therapy has proven successful in clinical trials regarding glioblastoma. Equally important are the hints suggesting peroxisome proliferator‐activated receptors (PPARs) ligands being co‐expressed in the central nervous system (CNS). This provides a rationale about investigating the possible synergistic effect of CIK cells and PPARs.

pmc-12610046.title: Biomechanical Comparison of Patient-Specific Temporomandibular Joint Prostheses Using Ti6Al4V and CoCrMo Alloys: A Finite Element Analysis
pmc-12610046.creator: Ezgi Yüceer-Çetiner, Yasin Doğu, Hakan Yurten, Altan Varol
pmc-12610046.description: End-stage temporomandibular joint (TMJ) disorders often necessitate total joint replacement, and the selection of biomaterial directly impacts long-term outcomes. Ti6Al4V and CoCrMo are commonly used alloys, yet their biomechanical performance in patient-specific prostheses remains insufficiently compared. This study aimed to evaluate the mechanical response of custom TMJ prostheses fabricated from these alloys using finite element analysis (FEA).

pmc-12658073.title: Biochemical, immune, and endocrine biomarkers associated with exacerbated muscular response: insights from a field-based operational cohort study
pmc-12658073.creator: Deivide Oliveira-de-Souza, Diego Viana Gomes, João Bosco Pesquero, Francisco Radler de Aquino Neto, Ricardo Luzardo, Beatriz Barreto-Duarte, Bruno B. Andrade, Andréia Carneiro
pmc-12658073.description: Muscle damage and systemic stress responses are common consequences of intense physical exertion. However, the extent to which these responses vary according to the severity of muscular strain remains unclear. We conducted a field-based study involving 24 active-duty elite military personnel who participated in five distinct operational missions in Brazil.

pmc-12743830.title: TROPION-Lung15: a randomized phase III study of osimertinib combined with datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) or Dato-DXd alone versus platinum-doublet chemotherapy in patients with EGFR-mutated advanced non-small cell lung cancer and whose disease has progressed on prior osimertinib
pmc-12743830.creator: Daniel Shao-Weng Tan, Ernest Nadal, Parneet Cheema, Yi-Long Wu, Myung-Ju Ahn, Junko Tanizaki, Ellie Grainger, Emily Nizialek, Alessandra Forcina, Toon van der Gronde, Helena A. Yu
pmc-12743830.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background:Osimertinib is the preferred treatment for patients with EGFR-mutated advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in several settings; however, disease progression is common, and treatment options after progression are limited. Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd), an antibody-drug conjugate comprising a humanized anti-trophoblast cell-surface antigen 2 (TROP 2) monoclonal antibody conjugated to a potent topoisomerase I inhibitor via a plasma-stable linker, has demonstrated efficacy in advanced NSCLC, including previously treated EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC.

pmc-12958955.title: Best Evidence Summary for Postoperative Pain Management in Adult ICU Patients
pmc-12958955.creator: Jie An, Xiang An, Bei Li
pmc-12958955.description: ObjectiveTo identify and summarize the best available evidence for postoperative pain management in adult intensive care unit (ICU) patients to inform clinical practice.MethodsUsing evidence-based nursing methodology, an evidence-based question on postoperative pain management in adult ICUs was formulated. A systematic literature search was conducted.

pmc-13138181.title: Long-term results of surgical management high-energy scapula fractures at a major trauma center
pmc-13138181.creator: Shoib Mahmood, Georgios Mamarelis, Mochamed Hachem, Adel Tavakkolizadeh, Karthik Karuppaiah, Toby Colegate-Stone
pmc-13138181.description: BackgroundScapular fractures are rare injuries typically resulting from high-energy trauma and often occur in polytrauma patients. Historically managed nonoperatively, recent trends in surgical intervention have evolved, particularly in major trauma centers (MTCs) where expertise and case volume have increased. However, there remains limited literature on the surgical management and long-term outcomes of these injuries.

pmc-13681445.title: Chemical-Specific Metabolic Disruption during Early Zebrafish Development is Modulated by the Microbiome
pmc-13681445.creator: Nanna Fyhrquist, Lydia Gugescu, Emma Wincent, Harri Alenius
pmc-13681445.description: Environmental contaminants such as per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, bisphenols, and agricultural fungicides are increasingly recognized as metabolic disruptors, yet how individual chemicals perturb metabolic pathways during early development remains incompletely understood. Here, we used targeted and untargeted metabolomics and pathway analysis in zebrafish embryos to characterize metabolic disruption induced by perfluorooctanesulfonic acid (PFOS), boscalid (BOS), and bisphenol F (BPF).
